creator: Alexander Terp
description:
When the window `$MUSTER_SOCKET` names has gone, pane verbs try the windows beside it and refuse if more than one answers, though only one of them draws the calling pane's tab. With `$MUSTER_SOCKET` unset they try none of them. In both cases `$MUSTER_PANE` is set, and the pane's daemon knows which window draws the pane.

## Measured

- **2026-10-01, devenv.** In a pane whose `$MUSTER_SOCKET` named a `window-<id>.sock` that no longer existed, `muster pane new` worked, but `pane wait --pane <new>` and `pane read` refused: "2 Muster windows are listening and nothing says which one this is about: .../window-release-<a>.sock, .../window-release-<b>.sock. Run this inside one of their panes, where $MUSTER_SOCKET names it, or pick one with --socket." The agent was inside a pane. Only one of the two windows drew its tab, and `--socket` with that one worked.
- **2026-10-05, devenv, 0.13.0.** After the agent's Claude Code session was resumed in the same pane, `$MUSTER_SOCKET` was unset while `$MUSTER_PANE` was still set. Why it was unset is not known; a launcher wrapper did the resume. `muster pane close` refused: "no Muster window is listening. $MUSTER_SOCKET is not set, so this is not running in a pane Muster made". Five `window-*.sock` files were under `~/.muster/daemon`; four did not answer and one drew the tab. Finding it took a loop over every socket.

## Things that might be true

- **When several windows answer, pick the one whose layout holds the calling pane** (or the target pane) instead of refusing.
- **With `$MUSTER_PANE` set and `$MUSTER_SOCKET` unset or gone, ask the pane's daemon which window draws the pane.**
- Say in the error that `$MUSTER_SOCKET` was stale, and do not say "not running in a pane Muster made" when `$MUSTER_PANE` is set.

Related: a_2YCgaUTuS (done) taught a pane whose window quit to try the windows beside it; this is the case where more than one answers.
title: 🔌 A pane with a stale or unset $MUSTER_SOCKET refuses when several windows answer
